Fix direction: lease >= BATCH x SEND_TIMEOUT_MS + margin (e.g. 2 minutes, matching STALE_CLAIM_MS), or renew the lease per iteration.

findings.title: The catchups-tick cron also fires nightly on the demo project, which has no wrong-deployment no-op and 401s if the demo lacks CRON_SECRET
findings.expected: Both Vercel projects build from this one repo and read the same vercel.json, so both schedule both crons; a cron that lands on the deployment it was not meant for should report success — exactly what /api/demo/reset's GET does for the production project ('200 rather than 404 so the nightly run reports success instead of raising a failed-cron alert every morning', demo/reset/route.ts:87-91).
findings.actual: GET /api/catchups/tick has no IS_DEMO branch: on the demo project it demands CRON_SECRET (line 27, fail-closed 401). If the demo project's env lacks CRON_SECRET, the demo's cron dashboard records a failing job every night at 02:00 UTC forever — permanent alert noise that trains the owner to ignore cron failures, on the project where a failing cron (the 20:00 reset) actually matters. If the secret IS set there, the tick runs the cron-wide sweep against the demo DB, which is harmless (Catchup/CatchupEdition/CatchupEntry are on the demo write allowlist, src/lib/demo.ts:74-79, and advanceDueCatchups swallows everything) but redundant beside the nightly reseed and the demo layout's own lazy tick.
findings.argument: vercel.json schedules both paths unconditionally; demo/reset/route.ts:87-91 documents the shared-vercel.json cross-fire problem and solves it for its own direction only. The tick route's doc comment discusses the secret and proxy allowlist but never the demo deployment, so the asymmetry looks like an oversight rather than a decision.
findings.proofPlan: Owner/orchestrator checks the demo Vercel project: (a) is CRON_SECRET set in its env, and (b) does the Crons tab show /api/catchups/tick failing nightly with 401. Code fix, if wanted, is three lines mirroring demo/reset: if (IS_DEMO) return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, skipped: "demo" }) before the secret check.

findings.title: credentialVersion session-revocation comparison has no test anywhere
findings.expected: The single mechanism that ends live JWT sessions on password reset, block, or deletion (audits M4/M5/H4) — `if (!dbUser || dbUser.isBlocked || (dbUser.credentialVersion ?? 0) !== (token.credentialVersion ?? 0))` — is pinned by at least one test, the way every other security invariant in this repo is (C1, C2, M1 all have tripwires).
findings.actual: Zero test files mention credentialVersion (grep across all 53 *.test.mjs: no hits). A flipped comparison (=== for !==), a dropped `dbUser.isBlocked` clause, or a refactor that stops selecting credentialVersion from the row would pass `npm run check`, CI, and every e2e spec. security-regressions.test.mjs pins the adjacent C1 shapes in the same file but never this line.
findings.argument: auth.ts lines 246/274/289/314 are the whole revocation loop: stamp at sign-in, compare on every session read. The comparison is pure logic on two nullable ints plus a boolean — exactly the shape this repo extracts into a testable module elsewhere (post-visibility-rule, human-pass-rule). Because it lives inline in the NextAuth callbacks, nothing imports it and nothing sweeps it, so the highest-value security comparison in the app is the least-guarded line in it. AGENTS.md advertises this mechanism as the reason JWT sessions are safe.
findings.proofPlan: Grep confirms absence (done: no test references credentialVersion). To prove the exposure: in a scratch worktree, change !== to === on auth.ts:314 and run node on every src/lib/*.test.mjs plus npx tsc --noEmit — all green. Fix direction: extract the predicate into src/lib/session-revocation.ts (pure) and pin blocked/version-bumped/null-token/legacy-row cases, or add a shape pin in security-regressions.test.mjs.

findings.title: composer-rule's B-048 editPost pin is vacuous: cityScope matches later functions in the same file
findings.expected: The assertion 'editPost drops cityScope again (B-048)' fails if editPost (feed/actions.ts:462-625) stops handling a resumed draft's cityScope.
findings.actual: The assertion tests `/cityScope/` against `feedActions.slice(indexOf("export async function editPost"))` — the tail of the WHOLE FILE from line 462 to EOF. cityScope appears at least 6 times after editPost's body ends (loadPosts:1044,1165; loadSavedPosts:1233,1283, comments at 1010/1230), so deleting editPost's entire cityScope handling leaves the test green. The fnBody() extraction that was supposed to scope it is computed and then discarded (`void fn;` at line 132).
findings.argument: fnBody() in this test slices to the first `\n  }` (a two-space-indented close), which truncates a top-level server action long before its real end, so the author fell back to the whole-tail slice and the regex now spans ~1000 unrelated lines. B-048's original shape was exactly the server half regressing while the client half (which the other two assertions in this test do pin: initialCityScope and formData.set in create-post-form.tsx) stayed correct — that split can recur with this test passing.
findings.proofPlan: Read src/lib/composer-rule.test.mjs:125-143 next to feed/actions.ts:462 and 1044. Mutation check in a scratch worktree: delete the cityScopeUpdate block (feed/actions.ts:550-...) and run `node src/lib/composer-rule.test.mjs` — it passes. Fix: extract editPost's body with the balanced-brace fnBody from gate-coverage.test.mjs and assert on that slice.

findings.title: gate-coverage's action discovery has three silent-skip vectors for a future ungated action
findings.expected: The sweep 'every exported server action is gated or deliberately public' (the H1/H3/L4 tripwire) sees every action file and every exported action, so a new ungated endpoint fails npm run check.
findings.actual: Three future shapes escape without failing anything: (1) line 106's filter `/^\s*(['"])use server\1/` requires the directive at byte 0 of the file — a header comment ABOVE "use server" (legal JS, valid Next) silently drops the whole file from the sweep, and this repo's house style is exactly such header comments (four files already quote the directive inside leading comments and are filtered out); (2) line 97's `git grep '"use server"'` never finds a single-quoted 'use server' directive; (3) exportedActions (line 58) matches only `export async function` — `export const f = async () =>` and `export { f }` forms are invisible, and an invisible action is treated as gated rather than failing.
findings.argument: All three fail OPEN: a file or export the discovery misses produces no assertion at all, so the exact class the test exists for (a new action where nobody thought about auth) ships silently. Verified that all 20 current action files lead with a double-quoted directive and use only `export async function` (greps run), so this is a regression vector, not a live hole — but the sweep's value is precisely the future action.
findings.proofPlan: Reproduce in a scratch worktree: create src/components/foo/actions.ts beginning with a block comment, then "use server", then an ungated `export async function leak()` — run node src/lib/gate-coverage.test.mjs: passes. Fix: filter with /^\s*(?:\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/\s*|\/\/[^\n]*\n\s*)*(["'])use server\1/, grep for both quote styles, and add const/arrow and export-list forms to exportedActions (or assert the file contains ONLY export-async-function exports, failing loud on anything else).

findings.title: check.mjs reports ESLint and the protocol audit as "clean" when the tool itself crashes
findings.expected: Each gate the runner reports on can actually reach its failure state: a gate whose underlying tool did not run says so rather than reporting clean.
findings.actual: The lint gate (lines 77-88) ignores the child exit code entirely and parses only the '(N problems (N errors, N warnings))' summary; when eslint crashes (config error, bad plugin — output is a stack trace, no summary), m is null, errors=warnings=0, ok=true, detail 'clean'. The protocol gate (lines 95-99) is identical: if scripts/qa/protocol-audit.mjs throws before printing 'N violation(s)' (verified it only prints that line, at its line 230), the match fails, n=0, ok=true, 'clean'. Both would report ok forever while enforcing nothing.
findings.argument: run() (line 37) captures {code, out} but lint and protocol destructure only out / only match on out. Both gates are non-blocking by design (documented), so the marginal harm is the false 'ok' label — but that label is what tells the operator the design-system enforcement exists at all; a crashed protocol-audit.mjs is zero enforcement wearing a green mark. types, lab and tests correctly use exit codes (verified: lab-audit exits 1 on stranded rooms, protocol-audit exits 1 on violations — but a crash exits nonzero with no parseable line).
findings.proofPlan: Safe demo without touching the repo: `node -e "..."` reproducing the parse (feed the lint regex a stack-trace string, observe errors=0). Or in a scratch worktree add `throw new Error('x')` at the top of protocol-audit.mjs and run npm run check: the protocol row prints 'ok ... clean'. Fix: treat a nonzero exit WITHOUT a parsed summary as a gate failure (soft or hard), never as clean.

findings.title: cascade-rule cannot catch a NEW communal model, though its header claims it "fails on the day it is written"
findings.expected: Per the header (lines 19-23): 'it walks every onDelete: Cascade foreign key out of User and asserts that no COMMUNAL container is reachable. A future model wired the same careless way fails here on the day it is written.'
findings.actual: The graph walk is real, but 'communal' is a hard-coded 4-name list: ["Group", "Catchup", "CatchupEdition", "CatchupPrompt"]. A future communal container that is a NEW model (an Events table, a shared album, a group wiki page) created with creatorId onDelete: Cascade from User is cascade-reachable and destroys other members' writing on account purge — and appears in casualties never, because it is not in COMMUNAL. The claim holds only for careless wiring that endangers the four existing names.
findings.argument: cascadeReachableFromUser() computes the full reachable set; the assertion then filters it through the fixed COMMUNAL allowset (line 96), so the test's sensitivity is bounded by a list a future author must remember to extend — the exact remembering-failure (B-070 style) this suite elsewhere derives away. The inverse assertion (line 115) has the same shape: a new own-content model is not required to cascade. The comment mis-describes the code, which per this audit's rules is itself the evidence.
findings.proofPlan: Code trace only: read lines 59-101. Thought-experiment mutation: add `model Event { id ... creator User @relation(fields:[creatorId], references:[id], onDelete: Cascade) ... }` to a scratch schema copy and run the test — passes. Fix direction: invert the default — assert the cascade-reachable set is a SUBSET of an explicit own-content allowlist, so any new reachable model fails until someone classifies it (fail-closed, same pattern as PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN).

findings.title: index-coverage's header claims it catches a forgotten index on a new relation; it checks a fixed 10-entry list
findings.expected: Header (lines 19-22): the test 'fails the moment somebody adds a relation and forgets its index' — i.e. the B-090 sequential-scan class cannot re-enter through a new table.
findings.actual: REQUIRED is a curated list of exactly the 10 relations the 2026-08 audit measured. A new child table added tomorrow (a reply-love, an event-RSVP) with the same leads-with-userId @@unique and no thingId index recreates the per-request full-table scan at 2k members, and no test examines it. Only edits to the 10 named model/column pairs can fail.
findings.argument: The parsing machinery (model(), leadsWith()) is generic and could walk every `fields: [xId]` relation in the schema the way cascade-rule walks onDelete — the restriction to a fixed list is the whole gap. The header sentence describes the generic version, not the shipped one; whoever extends the schema will read that sentence and reasonably believe the gate has their back.
findings.proofPlan: Code trace: lines 27-61 vs the header. Mutation: add an unindexed child model to a scratch schema and run the test — passes. Fix: derive the checked set from every @relation with fields: whose model also has interaction-shaped @@unique([userId, X]) pairs, with a small allowlist for relations deliberately left unindexed (each with its reason, PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN style); or at minimum correct the header to say it pins the audited ten only.

findings.title: C2 ownership-gate sweep pins 2 of the 3 write paths that accept image URLs; messages/actions.ts is unswept
findings.expected: The test named 'C2: every write path that accepts image URLs runs the ownership gate' covers every such path, so dropping the gate anywhere fails npm run check. The ownership gate is what stops the C2 critical (any member deleting every named R2 object, unrecoverably — no R2 versioning).
findings.actual: The sweep list is [feed/actions.ts, catchups/actions.ts]. src/app/(main)/messages/actions.ts also accepts a caller-supplied imageUrl into AdminMessage rows and calls ownedUploadUrls (lines 55, and again in the reply paths at ~140/182) — verified by grep — but is absent from the test. A refactor of the admin-thread composer that drops the ownership check regresses C2 on that path with every gate green.
findings.argument: grep -rln ownedUploadUrls src → feed, messages, catchups (three action files) against the test's two. The messages path is the newest of the three (admin-thread screenshots), which is exactly how a hardcoded list rots: it was written before or without the third path. Same class as the cascade/index findings but here the drift has ALREADY happened — the test's name promises coverage it no longer has.
findings.proofPlan: greps above settle the mismatch (done). Fix: add messages/actions.ts to the list, or better, derive the list — every file matching git grep -l 'imageUrl\|images' -- 'src/**/actions.ts' that writes prisma rows must contain ownedUploadUrls, with named exemptions.

findings.title: No test pins that interaction actions actually CALL the visibility guard (the H3 wiring)
findings.expected: H3's bug was five interaction paths acting on a postId without asking whether the caller could see the post. The pure rule (decidePostVisibility) is superbly tested (post-visibility-rule.test.mjs, 311 lines of attacks), and something should pin the WIRING — that every action taking a postId/commentId consults canViewPost/canViewPostOfComment — because the wiring, not the rule, is what actually broke.
findings.actual: No sweep exists. feed/actions.ts has 17 exported actions; 6 call canViewPost/canViewPostOfComment (lines 366, 635, 713, 757, 1316, 1398). A new interaction path added tomorrow (a reaction, a share, a report-with-quote) that takes a postId and skips the guard leaks private-group/city/batch content by id with every test green — the exact original H3 shape, and this codebase demonstrably grows such paths (toggleCommentLike was added for exactly this reason).
findings.argument: gate-coverage.test.mjs proves the repo already knows how to sweep action files for a required marker and force new exceptions onto a written list. The same machinery pointed at 'body mentions postId/commentId parameter ⇒ body must contain canViewPost|canViewPostOfComment or be on an exempt list (createPost, deletePost, loadPosts...)' would close the class. Its absence is the largest wiring invariant with no tripwire, second only to credentialVersion.
findings.proofPlan: Greps above establish the current call-site set (done). Demonstrate the gap: in a scratch worktree add `export async function echoPost(postId: string)` to feed/actions.ts that fetches and returns the post with only an auth() gate — gate-coverage passes (it has a gate), nothing else looks. Fix: a gate-coverage-style sweep in post-visibility-rule.test.mjs or its own file.

findings.title: check.mjs test discovery is extension- and location-bound: a renamed or relocated test silently stops running
findings.expected: The unit-test gate runs every test the repo holds, or fails loudly when one drops out of the run.
findings.actual: findTests() collects only files ending exactly '.test.mjs' under src/ and scripts/. A test renamed to .test.ts or .spec.mjs (a natural TS-migration or convention move), or placed in e2e/, prisma/, or a new top-level dir, is silently excluded; the gate then reports 'N/N passing' with a smaller N and no signal. There is no count pin and no manifest, so shrinkage is invisible unless someone remembers the old number (CLAUDE.md still says '14 unit tests'; there are 53).
findings.argument: The same session that wrote TRAPS' 'pin the property, not the instance' left the test RUNNER pinned to an instance (one extension, two roots). The failure is fail-open: exclusion produces passing output. Playwright specs are intentionally outside this gate (documented); the risk is unit tests drifting out by rename.
findings.proofPlan: Read findTests (lines 49-57) and line 116. Demonstrate: `git mv src/lib/db-text.test.mjs src/lib/db-text.spec.mjs` in a scratch worktree → npm run check reports one fewer test, still exits 0. Fix: also match .test.ts/.test.js, or assert a minimum count the way gate-coverage asserts files.length >= 15.

findings.title: avatar.test's distribution check exercises a hand-copied mirror of the hash, not avatar.ts
findings.expected: The distribution bands (species ±28%, colour ±15%, pose ±10% over 16k ids) constrain the REAL hash members' avatars are dealt from.
findings.actual: fnv1a/axisIndex/birdFor are re-implemented inside the test (lines 28-48) with copied salts ('species::' etc.), the '>>> 13' window and counts 50/10/4; the distribution block never calls avatar.ts. If avatar.ts's axisIndex changes salt, shift, or count, the mirror silently diverges and the bands keep validating the OLD algorithm. Only the reserved-birds block (lines 105-127) imports the real module, and it bounds the RANGE (never reaches Roller 50 or the Hoopoe index), not uniformity — a degenerate-but-in-range distribution regression passes everything.
findings.argument: The mirroring is deliberate and commented ('so a bug in avatar.ts cannot hide behind the same bug in its test') — sound for catching a shared-bug at birth, but it has no drift tripwire: nothing asserts mirror(seed) === real(seed) on even one sample, so the two implementations can part ways forever without a failure. avatar.ts even exports fnv1a (line 140), making a one-line parity assertion free.
findings.proofPlan: Code trace: avatar.test.mjs:28-48 vs avatar.ts:140-172 (verified identical today). Fix: add `for (const s of samples) assert.equal(birdFor(s).species, hashSpeciesFor(s))`-style parity over a few hundred ids, keeping the independent mirror AND pinning it to reality.

findings.title: email-normalization's negative-shape pins are spelling-bound; the B-020 raw-lookup bug can return under a different variable name
findings.expected: 'no sign-in path looks a member up by the address as typed' fails whenever authorize() or registerUser queries the unique email column with unnormalized input.
findings.actual: The pins refuse only two exact spellings: `findUnique({ where: { email }` (shorthand) in auth.ts and `where: { email: email }` in signup. A regression written as `where: { email: submitted }` or `where: { email: raw }` — the natural shape after any variable rename — matches neither negative regex, and the paired positive assertion (/acctKey/ merely existing somewhere in auth.ts) does not prevent it. The member-facing bug (an address stored with a capital can never reset or sign in) returns with the suite green.
findings.argument: Negative shape assertions can only refuse spellings they anticipate; this file's own B-020 history is three coexisting canonical forms, i.e. precisely the kind of drift a spelling pin cannot hold. The pure half (normalizeEmail/emailField) is genuinely behavioral and fine; the wiring half is the weak seam — same wiring-vs-rule split as the post-visibility finding.
findings.proofPlan: Code trace of lines 65-85 against src/lib/auth.ts's lookup. Mutation: rename the looked-up variable in a scratch worktree and drop normalizeEmail from the lookup — test passes. Fix: assert positively that the lookup goes through the normalized key (e.g. pin `where: { email: acctKey }` or an equivalent derived form), which fails loud on any respelling.

findings.title: /ingest PostHog reverse proxy forwards members' live session cookies to a third party
findings.expected: Analytics capture requests proxied through /ingest reach PostHog without the site's credentials; the session JWT never leaves rishivalley.space infrastructure.
findings.actual: Every /ingest request is a same-origin fetch, so the browser attaches all cookies including __Secure-authjs.session-token (a 30-day bearer JWT), and the external rewrite relays the request headers to eu.i.posthog.com. PostHog continuously receives valid session tokens for every signed-in member with analytics running.
findings.argument: posthog-js's bundled fetch sets no credentials option (grep of node_modules/posthog-js/dist/array.full.js finds no 'credentials:' / 'withCredentials'), and the fetch default is 'same-origin', which sends cookies on same-origin requests; /ingest is same-origin by design ('the browser talk only to rishivalley's own /ingest path'). The rewrite target is external (https://eu.i.posthog.com/:path*), and Next's external-rewrite proxy (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/proxy-request.js, httpxy with changeOrigin) rewrites only Host and adds x-forwarded-host — it does not strip Cookie. proxy.ts lists /ingest as public so signed-in members' requests pass straight through with cookies intact. Nothing in next.config.ts or proxy.ts strips the Cookie header for /ingest. A compromise of (or subpoena to) PostHog yields session takeover of every active member; credentialVersion revocation only helps after a password reset/block.
findings.proofPlan: Signed in on production, open DevTools > Network, select any /ingest/e or /ingest/decide request and confirm the Cookie request header carries the session token (proves the browser half). For the server half, either confirm Vercel's external-rewrite header forwarding in their docs, or locally run the dev server, temporarily point the /ingest catch-all rewrite at a request-capture endpoint, load a page while signed in, and read whether Cookie arrived. Fix direction if confirmed: route /ingest through a route handler (or middleware) that deletes the cookie header before forwarding.

findings.title: Letter page's raw isHidden check defeats the pinned author-exemption on hidden posts
findings.expected: Per the settled owner decision (docs/planning/bugs.md, 'the post visibility rule's author exemption sits ABOVE the hidden check... a test pins it'), the author of a moderator-hidden post can still open it to respond to the moderation. decidePostVisibility implements exactly that: author exemption at post-visibility-rule.ts:190, hidden check at :202.
findings.actual: For LETTERS the author gets a 404 on their own hidden letter: line 67 runs `if (!letter || letter.kind !== "letter" || letter.isHidden) notFound();` BEFORE canViewPost at line 88 ever runs, so the author exemption is unreachable on this surface. A hidden feed POST remains reachable to its author; a hidden letter does not. The two surfaces disagree.
findings.argument: The early return short-circuits on the raw Post.isHidden column with no author check. The comment directly beneath it (lines 68-86) argues 'One rule, not four hand-rolled checks... canViewPost... already exempts the author' — the exact drift the comment argues against is reintroduced by the line above it. Internal inconsistency proves it: generateMetadata in the SAME file (lines 25-43) guards with canViewPost only, so the author of a hidden letter gets the real letter title in the tab/history while the body 404s.
findings.proofPlan: Code trace is sufficient: post-visibility-rule.ts:183-202 shows author-exemption above hidden; letters/[id]/page.tsx:67 shows the pre-empting check. Live: with a test account, publish a letter, admin-hide it, open the direct link as the author — expect the hoopoe 404 (and the correct letter title in the browser tab); repeat with a hidden feed post via /feed, which stays visible to its author. Fix: drop `letter.isHidden` from line 67 and let canViewPost decide (it already returns not-ok for hidden to non-authors).
findings.taxonomy: route-gate divergence from shared visibility rule / settled-decision breach

findings.title: Expired or revoked session + deep link loses the destination: (main) layout redirects to /login without a next param
findings.expected: A member following a shared deep link (letter, profile, Catch-up round, notification email) signs in and lands on that destination — the behavior bug audit B-022 established when the proxy does the bounce (proxy.ts:263 sets ?next=pathname+search).
findings.actual: When the request CARRIES a session cookie that is expired or revoked (30-day JWT expiry, credentialVersion bump from a password reset or block), the proxy passes it through on cookie PRESENCE alone (proxy.ts:149-151, 'lightweight check'), and the (main) layout's real session check fails into a bare `redirect("/login")` — no next param — so after sign-in the member lands on /feed and the link they clicked is gone.
findings.argument: proxy.ts only appends `next` in the `!sessionCookie` branch (lines 256-264). The layout's failure branch at (main)/layout.tsx:24-26 is the path every stale-cookie request takes and it discards the pathname, which the layout could read from the x-pathname header the proxy already forwarded. Every member with a >30-day-old cookie who follows an emailed link — precisely the re-engagement case notification emails exist for — hits this.
findings.proofPlan: Live: sign in, capture the session cookie, invalidate it (wait for expiry is impractical — instead reset the test account's password to bump credentialVersion), then open /letters/<some-id> with the old cookie: observe the 307 chain ends at /login with no ?next, and post-login lands on /feed. Code trace alone is also conclusive: compare proxy.ts:256-264 with layout.tsx:24-26.

findings.title: /api/demo/reset is absent from publicPaths, so the real deployment's nightly cron never reaches the route's deliberate no-op
findings.expected: Per the route's own comment (src/app/api/demo/reset/route.ts:87-91): 'Both deployments build from this repo... both run this cron. On the real one it is a deliberate no-op: 200 rather than 404 so the nightly run reports success instead of raising a failed-cron alert every morning.' Both sibling crons (/api/catchups/tick, /api/retention/sweep) were explicitly added to publicPaths for exactly this cookie-less server-to-server GET shape.
findings.actual: On the real deployment (IS_DEMO false) the Vercel cron GET to /api/demo/reset carries no session cookie and /api/demo/reset is not in publicPaths, so the proxy answers 307 -> /login?next=/api/demo/reset before the route's GET handler (and its no-op 200) can run. The comment mis-describes what production does. Whether the owner sees a nightly failed-cron signal depends on whether Vercel's cron invoker follows the 307 (to /login's 200 HTML) or records the 3xx. It works on the demo only because the IS_DEMO proxy branch returns before the cookie check.
findings.argument: publicPaths (proxy.ts:203-247) lists /api/catchups/tick and /api/retention/sweep with comments naming this exact redirect problem, but not /api/demo/reset; vercel.json schedules /api/demo/reset at 20:00 UTC for every project built from this repo. isUnder/isPublic matching is exact/prefix so nothing else covers it. No data risk either way — the mismatch is between the code's stated intent and what the proxy does, plus possible nightly alert noise.
findings.proofPlan: Open the real (non-demo) Vercel project's cron logs and read the recorded status for the nightly /api/demo/reset invocation: a 307 (or a 200 whose response is the login page HTML) confirms the route handler never runs. Fix: add "/api/demo/reset" to publicPaths (the GET is CRON_SECRET-gated and the POST half is IS_DEMO-404 on the real site, so exposure adds nothing).

findings.title: Gated /api/* requests without a valid cookie get a 307-to-login HTML page instead of 401 JSON
findings.expected: A fetch() from app code to a member API (/api/places/search, /api/users/search, /api/users-by-batch, /api/upload/*) whose session has expired receives a machine-readable 401 so the client can show 'please sign in again'.
findings.actual: The proxy's unauthenticated branch redirects EVERY non-public path to /login, API routes included. fetch follows the 307, /login is public, so the client receives res.ok === true with HTML; res.json() then rejects with a SyntaxError. E.g. location-picker.tsx:162-171 does `res.ok ? res.json() : reject` and lands in its generic catch — the member typing in the city box after their cookie expired sees a generic failure with no hint that signing in would fix it.
findings.argument: proxy.ts:256-264 has no pathname.startsWith("/api/") distinction; the API routes' own 401 JSON answers (e.g. users/search/route.ts:16) are unreachable for cookie-less requests because the proxy intercepts first. The routes' careful 401/403/429 contracts only apply to requests that carry SOME session cookie. Members hit this whenever a tab outlives the 30-day JWT or a credentialVersion bump.
findings.proofPlan: curl -i 'https://rishivalley.space/api/places/search?q=delhi' with no cookie: expect 307 Location /login (not 401 JSON). In a browser, sign in, delete the session cookie via DevTools, type in the profile city picker: observe the request chain 307 -> /login 200 HTML and the picker's error state. Fix: in the !sessionCookie branch, answer pathname.startsWith('/api/') with NextResponse.json 401.
findings.taxonomy: auth-gate response shape / API vs page redirect

findings.title: robots.txt, sitemap.xml and .well-known/* are neither excluded from the matcher nor public, so crawlers get redirected to /login
findings.expected: On a public launch domain, GET /robots.txt answers a robots policy (or a clean 404), and standard well-known probes do not bounce into the auth flow; the public landing page is crawlable on its own terms.
findings.actual: No robots.ts/sitemap.ts exists (verified: only manifest.ts under src/app, nothing in public/), and the matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico, icon.svg, apple-icon.png, manifest.webmanifest, images/, uploads/. So /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /.well-known/* fall through to the !sessionCookie branch and 307 to /login?next=/robots.txt; a crawler following it reads the login page's HTML as the robots file.
findings.argument: publicPaths (proxy.ts:203-247) has no entry for any of these, the matcher (proxy.ts:320-324) does not exclude them, and no route or public file serves them. Google's spec parses the post-redirect HTML as an (empty) robots file — effectively allow-all — so crawling proceeds, but the site ships no crawl policy at all and every robots/well-known probe lands on the auth flow. Cosmetic with teeth on the eve of a public release.
findings.proofPlan: curl -i https://rishivalley.space/robots.txt (signed out): expect 307 to /login. Fix: add an app/robots.ts (and optionally sitemap.ts for the six public pages), which Next serves at /robots.txt, then either add the paths to publicPaths or the matcher exclusions.

findings.title: Bare /catchups/join (tokenless) falls through to the [catchupId] route instead of the join page's own dead-link shell
findings.expected: A truncated or hand-shortened invite link (/catchups/join with the token lost) shows the join page's purpose-built 'The invite link is not one we recognise' shell, which exists for exactly this case (src/app/catchups/join/[token]/page.tsx:82-97).
findings.actual: src/app/catchups/join/ defines only join/[token], so the one-segment path /catchups/join resolves to src/app/(main)/catchups/[catchupId]/page.tsx with catchupId="join": a signed-in member gets the generic hoopoe 404 (loadHome returns not-found); a signed-out visitor passes the proxy (exact publicPaths match "/catchups/join") only to hit the (main) layout's bare redirect("/login") — and per the layout finding above, without a next param.
findings.argument: Route-tree collision: publicPaths intends /catchups/join as the invite surface, but that URL exact-form belongs to the (main) dynamic segment because no page.tsx exists at src/app/catchups/join/. Prefix matching in the proxy ('/catchups/join/<token>') and the route tree disagree about who owns the bare path.
findings.proofPlan: Signed in, open /catchups/join: observe the generic 404 rather than the invite shell. Signed out, open it: observe the bounce to /login. Fix: add src/app/catchups/join/page.tsx rendering the same 'link not recognised' shell (or redirect to /catchups).

Prisma upsert atomicity: upsertCatchupPref carries a manual P2002 retry claiming 'upsert is a read-then-write inside Postgres', but submitEntry's upsert and setReminderPref's upsert have no such retry. If Prisma 7 with the pg adapter emits native INSERT..ON CONFLICT for these (both wheres are single compound uniques, so they should qualify), the retry is dead code and the others are fine; if it does NOT, concurrent autosave blurs in submitEntry can surface 'Something went wrong' on a save that worked. Needs one runtime look at the emitted SQL - orchestrator can settle it with query logging.

actions.ts loadFreshEdition advances the edition BEFORE the membership check, so any verified member can trigger clock transitions + notification fanout for a group they are not in by calling any edition-taking action with a foreign editionId. Latent trap if SessionProvider/useSession is ever added: @auth/core/lib/actions/session.js's catch (JWTSessionError) responds with sessionStore.clean() — an expired Set-Cookie — whenever the session callback throws, and this app's session callback does a Prisma read that throws on pool exhaustion/DB blips. Unreachable today only because nothing fetches that endpoint.

authorize() accepts an unbounded-length email string: normalizeEmail and the Upstash keys are built from it before any length check (recordLoginAttempt slices at 200 but the rate-limit key does not). Bounded by request rate; noted for the DoS-focused agent, not filed.

purgeUserAccount's 30s transaction ceiling means a member whose cascade cannot finish in 30s is never purgeable: the sweep retries them nightly forever, burning 30s and logging purge:<id> errors each night with no escalation path. Needs live sizing of the heaviest member's row count to judge.

Export's paged() generator: if the exact keyset boundary row is deleted mid-walk (member deletes a post during their own export), Prisma's cursor-on-missing-row returns empty and the section silently truncates while the JSON still parses clean.

User.coverPhoto is now writer-less and reader-less outside /lab (settings cover picker removed), yet purge and merge code still maintain it — a simplify-pass candidate, and the recent Low 106 fix it carries is effectively dead code.

drainPendingImagePurges' failure path (account-purge.ts:338-341) lacks the .catch the success-path delete has: a concurrent drain that already removed the row makes the attempts-increment update throw P2025, which propagates out of purgeUserAccount AFTER the account was successfully deleted (the drain call sits outside the try), turning a completed admin delete into a 500 with no audit entry written.

Ops, not code: if RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset in production, every event 500s by design, but Razorpay retries an individual event for only ~24h and auto-disables a persistently failing webhook — so the 'retry until configured' comfort in the route comment holds only for short windows. loadDirectoryPage's `loaded` param: Math.trunc(NaN/Infinity) survives to Prisma's skip if React flight encoding delivers non-finite numbers — worth a 30-second check that a crafted action call cannot 500.

directorySortOptions/directoryDefaultSort in src/lib/directory-facets.ts have no callers since the sort UI was removed — dead exports advertising a 'best-match' value directoryOrderBy treats as default; trim or reconnect.

AUTHOR_IN_GOOD_STANDING (src/lib/posts.ts:61) checks only author.isBlocked, not deletionRequestedAt: during a member's 60-day deletion grace window their posts/letters/comments stay visible while the directory, search and (probably) their profile hold them out — the same list-vs-link disagreement audit Low 78 fixed for blocked members. Content-policy territory, not scale; verify whether the profile 404s for deletion-pending accounts and whether the asymmetry is an owner decision.

verificationMailState (email-queue.ts:890-901) checks the daily budget BEFORE scheduling a targeted send, and claimAndSend never re-checks it: N unconfirmed members' simultaneous first page views can each pass the check and overshoot DAILY_CAP by ~N, eating the 5-message safety margin on launch morning. Self-healing (Resend 429 → quota deferral to midnight) but worth the mail-territory finder confirming the margin holds at realistic launch concurrency.

Vercel Analytics Hobby-tier event cap vs ~1.2M pageviews/month at the 2k target — same quota class as the PostHog finding; I could not verify the current Hobby quota offline. Recording stops silently at the cap.

Bell/comment keyset cursors share the vanished-cursor-row shape reported for the feed (notifications/actions.ts:30 — a cursor row the 100-cap prune or 365d sweep deleted; feed/actions.ts:1405 — a root comment whose visibility flips). Folded into finding 2; the fix session should sweep all keyset call sites, not just loadPosts.

Letters index pagination keys on createdAt alone (`createdAt: { lt: olderThan }`, letters/page.tsx:75-76): two letters sharing one millisecond across a page boundary would drop one. Millisecond ties are near-impossible organically; noting only so a future bulk-import (which writes many rows in one ms) knows the edge exists.

Did not audit: the demo deployment's reset path and seed volume, /lab routes, client bundle size, or the e2e/visual tooling — outside this charter's request-path lens. Upstash and Vercel Analytics exact current quota numbers need an online check by the orchestrator.

adminRemovePost hides a post but leaves its image bytes publicly fetchable at their R2 URLs forever — the exact argument adminRemovePhoto makes for deleting bytes on hide (audit M11) applies to post images and was not carried over. Outside my input-validation charter; a moderation-effectiveness gap worth its own look.

adminUpdateNote (profile/admin-actions.ts:121) and the adminRemovePost/adminRemoveComment 'note' arguments have no length cap; the note lands in User.adminNote and Notification.message (unbounded text, member-rendered). Admin-only writers, so low risk, but the only uncapped human-typed strings left.
adminVerifyUser's 'method' parameter is a compile-time union with no runtime check — a crafted admin call can write any string into verifyMethod, which the profile renders. Admin-only.

reportSchema in validators.ts:283 is dead code (report-action.ts validates inline); a future caller importing the schema by name would get different rules than the live path — drift hazard, candidate for deletion.
editPost carries no rate limit while createPost is metered ('posts', M2); each edit does several queries plus revalidatePath. Likely deliberate M2 scope (creation only) but unrecorded.

getNotifications' KEEP-prune comment claims scrolling can never delete rows under its own cursor, which is true for one device but not for a second device's first-page open (folded into the cursor finding as a site; the comment's scope claim is the lead).
The 'search' rate bucket (120/min) is generous for places/search's raw 234k-row scan even after a length cap is added; worth revisiting the token count for that one endpoint at 2k users.

Catch-up answers save only on blur/advance (answer-card.tsx flushBody): closing the tab or killing the app with focus still in the field silently loses the typed answer — the same class as the letters-desk finding but with no localStorage belt at all; letters got one (B-043), catch-ups did not. Worth one decision for both surfaces (flush on pagehide).

Admin cursor paginators not audited for the M36 stale-page guard: admin/people/people-list.tsx (loadMorePeople with params + cursor + rows.length) and admin/content/content-list.tsx — admin-only blast radius, but the same filter-change-mid-flight race shape as the Collection finding; a validator should scan both.

ambient-leaves.tsx recycle timers (window.setTimeout at lines ~291 and ~506, scheduled from inside the rAF loop) are not cancelled on unmount — landing page only; check whether spawn/capturePileLeaf touch dead DOM refs after navigation.

NotificationBell: a 'Load more' in flight across a panel reopen can append its old page and set a stale nextCursor after handleOpen reset the first page (dedupe hides duplicates but the cursor may skip/repeat a page). Small panel, low stakes; noting for completeness.

Not exhaustively examined (ran out of territory, not time): admin/** client components beyond the two named, settings/dark-gauntlet + nightfall + lights-on, mascot/moments/* and mascot-flight-layer internals, tour-panel/tour-spotlight full read (cleanup scan only), ui primitives (dialog/select/tabs/dropdown — shadcn/base-nova, low risk), forgot/reset password clients, trivia-gate, demo-bar, get-in-touch/admin-profile-tools, and all of src/app/lab/** (dev-only by charter).

CRON_SECRET presence is owner-owned and unverifiable from code: project memory records it as still owed. Until set on the production Vercel project + GitHub repo secret, /api/catchups/tick 401s nightly (masked by the layout's lazy tick) and retention.yml fails loudly every night. Orchestrator should get the owner to confirm it is now set in BOTH Vercel projects and GitHub.

Turnstile on preview deployments: NODE_ENV=production there, so the real env key pair is used; if the Cloudflare site key's hostname allowlist does not include *.vercel.app preview hosts the widget errors, no token is produced, and sign-in/signup on previews is refused (fail-closed on missing token). Tooling-facing only, but worth one preview-deployment sign-in check.

src/proxy.ts:154-156 comment claims the landing page 'stays statically rendered for logged-out visitors' — contradicted by the settled theme-cookie decision that makes every route dynamic. Consequence nil (the redirect logic is right); stale comment only.

next.config.ts PostHog rewrite comment says the proxying 'costs a few extra function invocations' — external rewrites are served by the platform proxy, not functions; harmless inaccuracy in a cost argument.

/api/demo/reset's runReset builds a bare `new PrismaPg({ connectionString })` with pg defaults (max 10, NO checkout timeout, no query_timeout) — the exact defaults src/lib/prisma.ts calls dangerous. Demo-only blast radius and one call a night, but a hung demo DB would pin that invocation to the platform duration cap with no client-side bound.

settings avatar action reads 'up to 15MB' per its own comment but the platform 413s anything over ~4.5MB before the action runs — unreachable headroom in production, only real locally. Verify the crop dialog's canvas output stays comfortably under 4.5MB on a phone-resolution source (I did not trace the canvas export dimensions).

The default Vercel max duration for these two projects (Fluid vs legacy, Hobby vs Pro) is a dashboard fact I cannot read from the repo; the drain-pass and finalize worst cases in my findings assume the ~60s order of magnitude the audit brief states. Orchestrator: confirm the plan/Fluid setting once, which also settles how much headroom after() work really has.

Top untested invariants beyond the findings, ranked (3-10 after credentialVersion #1 and visibility-wiring #2 which are filed as findings): (3) mail drain budget arithmetic and QueueLease mutual exclusion (email-queue.ts:385 dailyBudget, :612 takeDrainLease) — shape-pinned only, acknowledged as needing a DB; DAILY_CAP=95/RESET_RESERVE=20 arithmetic has no pure extraction; (4) purge collectImageUrls (account-purge.ts:96) vs schema drift — no sweep ties the schema's image-URL-bearing columns to the collector, so a NEW image column tomorrow orphans R2 bytes silently (TRAPS' exact fear); only AdminMessage.imageUrl is pinned; (5) proxy.ts publicPaths (line 203) — the signed-out route allowlist, the auth boundary itself, has no pin while the demo's closed list does; (6) CRON_SECRET bearer comparison on /api/catchups/tick, /api/retention/sweep, /api/demo/reset — untested; a dropped check makes the retention purge publicly triggerable; (7) razorpay.ts verifyWebhookSignature/verifyCheckoutSignature (lines 131-165) — pure, money-path, zero tests; also verify hmacMatches tolerates a wrong-length signature without timingSafeEqual throwing; (8) registerUser's full signup transaction (trivia gate, Turnstile, dedupe, joinBatchGroup) — only fragments pinned (P2002 answer, email field source); (9) per-IP trivia and ENQUEUE_LIMIT rate limiters — constants exist, no behavioral test; (10) storage.ts keyForUrl parsing — C2 shape-pinned but the parser itself has no unit test despite being nearly pure.

Group.coverImage (schema.prisma:234, 'Collection or upload') is not in collectImageUrls and not cleared by the purge the way User.coverPhoto deliberately is (account-purge.ts:231 handles coverPhoto only): if a member's own upload became a group cover, purging that member may delete the R2 object out from under a surviving communal group (dangling cover), or leave bytes unowned. Needs a trace by whoever owns the purge/storage territory.

CI ordering: check.yml runs on push to main, but a push already IS the Vercel deploy (both projects autodeploy), so the CI gate can only flag a bad commit after it is live — it cannot stop it. Possibly accepted ops posture; worth one deliberate sentence in OPERATIONS.md if so.

valley-day's sweep cannot see two adjacent escape hatches: a date rendered through bare toLocaleString (deliberately excluded as 'almost always a number') or through a module-level Intl.DateTimeFormat — and TRAPS itself pushes the next perf pass toward module-level Intl construction, which would walk the date formatting straight out of the sweep. No current violation (verified); future-shaped.
demoWriteAllowed('Photo','delete') is untested (create/update pinned only); confirm the model-closed branch refuses delete too — one assert.

The mail-policy 'outlives a single drain pass' test hardcodes ONE_PASS_MS=30_000 as an assumption about the drain's duration rather than deriving it from email-queue.ts's actual pass bound; if the drain's batch size or per-send timeout grows past 30s the property silently stops meaning what it says.

check.mjs runs all ~53 test files concurrently via Promise.all, each a full node process, several of which shell out to git grep — near the machine's documented OOM edge when combined with other gates (TRAPS: check + subagent gate = exit 137). If test count keeps growing, a small concurrency cap keeps the gate off that cliff.

gate-coverage's fnBody angle-bracket scanner miscounts a `=>` inside a generic return-type annotation (e.g. Promise<Array<() => void>>): the arrow's '>' decrements angle depth, which would make it skip the real body brace. No current signature has that shape; would fail loud (body null → ungated) rather than silent, so noted only for whoever edits the parser.

Vercel-edge behavior for '//'-prefixed and percent-encoded (%2F) paths cannot be proven from source on this machine: one signed-out curl each against production (//feed and /%2Ffeed) would confirm the 308-normalization happens before anything renders there too.

Whether Vercel's cron invoker follows a 307 (finding 4's consequence) and whether Vercel's edge forwards the Cookie header on external rewrites (finding 1's production half) both need the orchestrator's live/dashboard check; the in-repo mechanisms are proven.

Admin demotion mid-session: requireAdminPage runs in the admin layout on server renders, but a just-demoted admin's client-side router cache may serve already-fetched admin RSC segments until eviction; admin mutations re-check the role so writes are safe. Whether a role change bumps credentialVersion (which would end the session outright) belongs to the auth-territory agent.

The (main) layout awaits advanceDueCatchups + notification count + verificationMailState + touchLastSeen on every authenticated page render and schedules drainMailQueue after every response — the 2k-user load profile of that fan-out is load/perf territory, not route-map.

Two committed collection seed images carry U+202F (narrow no-break space) in their filenames (public/images/collection/'WhatsApp Image 2026-05-13 at 7.37.16 am.jpeg'); they are referenced from src/lib/demo-seed/content.ts — a validator could confirm the seeded URLs percent-encode that character consistently, else those demo photos 404.

DEMO_CLOSED_APIS has no mirror or pin test (unlike DEMO_CLOSED_PATHS); it is proxy-only so it cannot drift against a twin, but any future dangerous /api prefix on the demo is born OPEN at layer 1 and relies wholly on the Prisma default-deny — worth one line in the demo spec.

requestAccountDeletion success is followed by a client-side signOut (letterhead-profile.tsx:1353); if that POST fails the member stays signed in with a deletion scheduled — likely harmless (grace window, sign-in cancels), but the deletion-flow agent should confirm the UX.

publicPaths' prefix matching makes /login/<anything>, /privacy/<anything> etc. public; they 404 harmlessly today, but a future nested route under an (auth) or (policies) path would be born public — no current route is affected.
